bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar MBBS BDS Round 3 Allotment 2026: Reporting Dates & Documents | MedAdmit
bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB) has released the Round 3 provisional seat allotment for undergraduate medical and dental programmes on October 14, 2026. Candidates who have been allotted a seat in MBBS, BDS, BVSc & AH, or BFSc must now complete document verification and admission reporting within a strict two-day window. This round opened with 618 MBBS and 23 BDS vacant seats across government and private colleges in Bihar, making it a significant opportunity for waiting-list candidates to secure a medical seat. Allotted candidates must report for document verification and admission on October 16 or 17, 2026 at their designated centre, or risk forfeiting their seat. Unlock My College List When and Where to Report for Your Allotted Seat The reporting window for Round 3 allotment is strictly limited to October 16 and 17, 2026. There is no extension announced, and candidates who fail to report within these two days will lose their allotted seat. Each candidate will have been assigned a specific reporting centre based on their allotment; this information is available in the allotment order downloaded from the BCECEB portal. Document verification and provisional admission will be completed at the reporting centre during these two days. It is essential to plan your travel and arrange all required documents well in advance, as missing even one document can result in cancellation of your allotment. How to Download Your Round 3 Allotment Order Your allotment order is available on the official BCECEB portal at bceceboard.bihar.gov.in. The download window remains open from October 14 to October 17, 2026, so you have until the end of your reporting day to retrieve it. To access your allotment order, visit the BCECEB website, locate the UGMAC 2026 Round 3 allotment link on the homepage, and log in using your application number and date of birth. Once logged in, you will see your allotted college, course, and category details. Download the allotment order PDF and print it—you will need to carry this printout to the reporting centre. bihar_raw_news.title: CtrlS invests ₹10000 crore in Bihar for 150 MW AI facility - ET Datacenters
bihar_raw_news.content: Investments & Deals 1 min Read CtrlS invests ₹10,000 crore in Bihar for 150 MW AI facility CtrlS Datacenters will invest ₹10,000 crore in Bihar to establish a 150 MW hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) facility in Bodh Gaya. The company also inaugurated a ₹400 crore Patna data center with an initial 12 MW IT load, expanding its presence in eastern India. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 15, 2026 at 08:00 AM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights CtrlS to invest ₹10,000 crore for a 150 MW AI facility in Bodh Gaya, Bihar. Company inaugurated a ₹400 crore, 12 MW IT load data center in Patna. The Patna facility supports AI and cloud workloads for eastern India. Bihar government signed an LoI with CtrlS for the proposed investment. CtrlS Datacenters Ltd will invest ₹10,000 crore in Bihar to construct a 150 MW hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) facility in Bodh Gaya . The company has signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with the Government of Bihar for this proposed investment. This expansion includes the inauguration of a ₹400 crore data center in Patna . The Patna facility, located in the Patliputra Industrial Area, has an initial IT load of 12 MW. This facility supports AI and cloud workloads for enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers, and technology companies across Bihar and eastern India . Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the Patna facility on October 13, 2026. CtrlS founder and CEO Sridhar Pinnapureddy stated the company aims to build a stronger IT ecosystem in Bihar. He credited the state government's policy environment, business climate, and incentives for supporting the investment. The new data center incorporates disaster-resilient infrastructure, military-grade security, and energy-efficient systems, according to CtrlS. The company plans to establish more than 20 edge data centers across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India in the coming years. CtrlS operates 19 data centers across nine key Indian markets and plans to build over 4.4 GW of capacity by 2030. Comments What are your thoughts?

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Regional News 30 Former Prez Kovind releases Hindi edition of autobiography in Lucknow, praises UP’s progress unde...
national_raw_news.content: Former President Ram Nath Kovind praised the efforts in Uttar Pradesh in development, law and order, and good governance under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s leadership. The former President was addressing the release ceremony of the Hindi edition of his autobiography, ‘Bharatiya Ganatantra Ki Vijaygatha, Mera Jeevan, Mera Sangharsh ‘, at a function in Lucknow. He said that the state had gained fresh momentum after the government was formed under Yogi Adityanath’s leadership in 2017. The Chief Minister has resolved to make Uttar Pradesh a one trillion dollar economy and has given unprecedented momentum to efforts to transform the state into an Uttam Pradesh, in line with the dreams of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He expressed confidence that the development schemes being implemented in the state would extend opportunities for employment, education and economic progress to all sections of society. Sharing memories of his childhood, Ram Nath Kovind said that his house in the village of Paraunkh in Kanpur Dehat was extremely modest, and water used to leak through the roof during the rainy season. After being elected President in 2017, he thought of those families who still dream of a better future. Through the efforts of the Modi government at the Center and the Yogi government in Uttar Pradesh under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, poor families have not only received pucca houses but have also gained dignity and security. Only those who have lived under a leaking roof can truly understand the importance of a pucca house. The former President called on the youth of Uttar Pradesh to participate actively in politics, governance, administration, and public life. He said that participation in democracy should not remain limited to voting. For good governance, honest, capable, and sensitive people must come forward in politics. He urged young people to serve the nation and conveyed the message that they should never give up.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Regional News 40 Government constitutes committee to examine issues raised by sugarcane farmers
national_raw_news.content: The Government has constituted a committee to examine issues raised by sugarcane farmers and recommend appropriate measures for addressing their concerns. Former Member of NITI Aayog, Professor Ramesh Chand, will chair the committee, which includes the Agriculture Commissioner, Joint Secretary (Sugar), Department of Food and Public Distribution and Joint Secretary (Legal Metrology), Department of Consumer Affairs, as members. The constitution of the Committee follows the decisions taken during a meeting of representatives of sugarcane farmers from Karnataka and Maharashtra with the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and the Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the Committee will consult all stakeholders, including farmers’ representatives, sugar mill associations, State Governments and other experts. The Committee will submit its report, containing its findings and specific recommendations, as early as possible, for consideration by the competent authority. The Committee will examine the demand for an increase in remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers, taking into account cultivation costs and other relevant factors. It will also examine the demand for revision of the ex-mill Minimum Selling Price of sugar in the context of sugar production costs, market realisations, and the financial viability of sugar mills. Other key areas of examination will include existing mechanisms for testing and reporting sugar recovery and prevailing sugarcane weighment practices at sugar mills. The Committee will also examine prevailing practices relating to deductions from the weight of mechanically harvested sugarcane and assess any actual losses arising from mechanised harvesting. It will evaluate the financial impact of the present practices on the cane price payable to farmers and may consider any other related matters deemed necessary.

national_raw_news.title: Puducherry’s Lycée Français International celebrates 200 years of educational heritage 50 mins ago 23
national_raw_news.content: Puducherry’s Lycée français international de Pondicherry (pronounced as ‘lee-SAY frahn-SHE international de Pondicherry’), one of the oldest French schools outside France still in operation, is celebrating its bicentenary today, marking two centuries of educational and cultural history in the Union Territory. Founded in 1826 as the Collège royal de Pondichéry by French Governor Eugène Desbassayns de Richemont (spelt as uh-ZHEN day-bah-SEHN duh reesh-MOHN), the institution has evolved through successive political and social changes, retaining its place in Puducherry’s educational heritage and its links with both French and Indian communities. The week-long bicentenary celebrations feature exhibitions, cultural performances, historical presentations and alumni reunions. More than 400 former students, many travelling from France, are participating in the celebrations, while over 1,000 guests are expected to attend the official ceremony this evening. French Ambassador to India, Thierry Mathou (pronounced tye-REE Ma-too), Director General of the Agency for French Education Abroad Alexandre Morois (Alexandre Mo-Reez), Puducherry Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan and Chief Minister N. Rangasamy will also participate in the bicentenary celebrations. Established at a time when colonial society was marked by racial and caste divisions, the school was initially reserved for white boys. Access gradually expanded over the following decades. Its educational activities also evolved, with the introduction of Indian languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Bengali, alongside specialised courses and opportunities for higher studies in France. Today, the Lycée français international de Pondichéry has more than 400 students, from kindergarten to the final year of secondary education. It is part of the Agency for French Education Abroad network, which comprises 640 schools in 140 countries, and has an international alumni network of nearly 7,000 former students. The bicentenary has also inspired 23 projects involving students and the school community, covering historical research, archival work, artistic expression and digital creations.
